attacks.reason: The internal ribbing may not provide sufficient mechanical interlock to counteract cyclic masticatory forces.
attacks.evidence_required: Finite element analysis or experimental testing to validate the mechanical interlock of the internal ribbing.

attacks.reason: The transfer from 3D printing to mechanical interlock is not clearly justified.
attacks.evidence_required: A clear explanation of the relationship between 3D printing and mechanical interlock, or experimental evidence to support the transfer.

attacks.reason: The inventive device fails under high cyclic masticatory forces or in cases of material fatigue.
attacks.evidence_required: Experimental testing to determine the threshold of cyclic masticatory forces that the inventive device can withstand, and a study on the effect of material fatigue on the internal ribbing.

attacks.reason: The combination of 3D printing and internal ribbing is not an obvious combination for an expert in the field.
attacks.evidence_required: Expert testimony or a survey of experts in the field to determine the obviousness of the combination.

attacks.reason: Existing references disclose similar internal ribbing designs for implant-abutment interfaces.
attacks.evidence_required: A patent search or literature review to identify existing references that disclose similar internal ribbing designs.

attacks.reason: The inventive device can be built using existing 3D printing technology and titanium alloy materials.
attacks.evidence_required: A detailed description of the manufacturing process and materials used to build the inventive device.

attacks.reason: The inventive device's performance is difficult to measure and compare to existing devices.
attacks.evidence_required: A clear and measurable metric to evaluate the performance of the inventive device, and a comparison to existing devices to demonstrate its superiority.

refinement_needed: Refine the mechanism to improve mechanical interlock, provide clear justification for the transfer, and address the boundary conditions. Additionally, conduct a thorough patent search and literature review to identify existing references and improve the inventive device's performance metrics.
